candidates.name: Sebilj
candidates.content: Pseudo-Ottoman wooden fountain in the middle of an open square in the old town of Sarajevo. It was built by Mehmed Pasha Kukavica in 1753, and under Austro-Hungarian rule moved to its current location in 1891 by Austrian architect

candidates.name: Sacred Heart Cathedral
candidates.content: The largest Christian cathedral in Bosnia, and the seat of Archbishop of Vrhbosna. It was built in honour of the Sacred Heart of Jesus in a Neo-Gothic style with Romanesque Revival elements, and modelled on the Notre-Dame of Dijon

candidates.name: Brusa Bezistan
candidates.content: Small museum in a 1551 Ottoman silk shop, tracing Sarajevo's development from prehistory through Roman, Ottoman, Austro-Hungarian and modern times. Its centrepiece is a model of the Old Town on the ground floor, made by Husein Kar

candidates.name: National Museum
candidates.content: Static displays of the natural and human history of Bosnia and Herzegovina, including an exhibition of traditional Turkish-style homes of Sarajevo prevalent in the nineteenth century, an extensive collection of insects and stuffed

candidates.name: Sarajevo Museum 1878–1918
candidates.content: A small museum dedicated to the Austro-Hungarian occupation of Sarajevo, which started with the Berlin Congress in 1878 and ended with World War I in 1918. The exhibition portrays life in the Austro-Hungarian era from different pe

candidates.name: Svrzo's House
candidates.content: Part of the Sarajevo City Museum, Svrzo's House shows the living conditions of a Muslim family at the end of the 17th century. The house was built by the eminent Sarajevo family Glođo during the Ottoman occupation of the city, but

candidates.name: Gazi Husrev-Bey's Library Museum
candidates.content: In a modern building opened in 2014, the museum has a collection of over 1,200 items, displaying Islamic calligraphy, time-keeping and everyday objects of Muslim life. It's within the library which holds some 100,000 historic manu

candidates.name: Tunnel of Hope
candidates.price: 15 KM. 5 KM for students. Additional charge for an audio guide delivered via your smartphone
candidates.content: Sarajevo was besieged and bombarded from 1992, and by 1993 the blockade was total. Serb forces seized the airport, but handed it over to UN peacekeeping forces to avert international intervention. The UN used the airport to bring

candidates.name: War Childhood Museum
candidates.content: Opened in 2017, the museum has personal belongings on display that illustrate the experience of a childhood during the Siege of Sarajevo. An audio guide reveals the stories behind the items, complementing the exhibits with additio

candidates.name: Museum of crimes against humanity and genocide 1992-1995
candidates.alt: Muzej zločina protiv čovječnosti i genocida 1992-1995
candidates.content: Small but important museum about the genocide during the Bosnian Civil War of 1992-95. The human side of the conflict is portrayed with shocking pictures, personal testimonies and video. Complementary to the 11/7/95 Gallery, which

candidates.name: Gallery 11/07/95
candidates.content: A small but compelling exhibition about the Srebrenica Massacre of July 1995, when 8,372 people were killed. Events are described from the perspective of investigative journalists visiting the site of the genocide. The audio guide

candidates.name: Sniper Alley
candidates.content: Sniper Alley was the informal name primarily for streets Zmaja od Bosne Street (Dragon of Bosnia Street) and Meša Selimović Boulevard, the main boulevard in Sarajevo which during the Bosnian War was lined with snipers' posts, and

candidates.name: Bosnian Historical Museum
candidates.content: The museum was founded 70 years ago, but heavily damaged by shelling during the war and still in a perpetual state of disrepair. The exhibitions primarily focus on the war, but the presentation of the artifacts is outdated, and th

candidates.name: Museum of Literature & Performing Arts
candidates.content: A small museum dedicated to the importance of literature and expressive arts in Sarajevo, with attention to prominent local writers and poets. Worth a visit to those interested in arts and literature.

candidates.name: Gazi Husrev-beg's Mosque
candidates.content: Beautiful medieval mosque at the heart of Old Town. Non-Muslims welcome, but dress appropriately and respect prayer times. It was built in 1530 / 1531 AD (937 AH) in what's called "classical Ottoman" or "early Istanbul" style. It

candidates.name: Jewish Museum
candidates.content: This is housed in the Old Temple (Il kal vjezu) or Grand Temple (Il kal Grandi) built in 1581 for the Sephardic settlers. It's a three-nave building with the front area used for preaching and the upper floors for the women's secti

candidates.name: Museum of the 105th Motorized Brigade
candidates.content: A memorial dedicated to the 105th Motorized Brigade of the Bosnian Army, which took part in the defense of Sarajevo during the 1992-95 siege of the city. Since 1993, over 7,000 members have passed through the brigade, of which 312

candidates.name: National Gallery
candidates.content: Established in 1946 after the Second World War, the National Gallery contains over 6,000 pieces of art, with a focus on works of Bosnian interest. Interestingly, the gallery remained open and held exhibitions during the Siege of S

candidates.name: Modern Art Museum
candidates.content: Museum for contemporary art, formed during the war as a "resistance of culture". It has 130 works by notable artists such as Italian painter and art theorist Michelangelo Pistoletto, Greek artist Jannis Kounellis, German performan

candidates.name: Despić House
candidates.content: A dependency of the Sarajevo City Museum, constructed in several stages during different periods, the oldest parts dating back to the 17th century. The property belonged to the wealthy Serb Orthodox Christian Despić family, which

candidates.name: Presidency Building
candidates.content: The Territorial Government Building (today, the official residence of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina) was designed by Josip Vancas and opened in March 1886. The building is modeled after Florentine Medici Ricardi Palace

candidates.name: Hanikah
candidates.content: A khanaqah is a Sufi lodge or centre for the study of Islamic mysticism. This one is a 1998 replica of the original built in 1531 with 14 study rooms, a simahana (room used for Dervish religious ritual), mihrab niche to indicate t

candidates.name: St Anthony's Church
candidates.content: Roman Catholic church in Gothic Revival style, built 1912-14 on the site of previous versions. The current interior dates from 1960s, with works by leading 20th C artists including Meštrović. The church serves the adjacent monaste

candidates.name: Cathedral Church of the Nativity of the Theotokos
candidates.content: The Cathedral is the largest Serbian Orthodox church in Sarajevo and one of the largest in the Balkans. It is dedicated to the nativity of the Theotokos, and erected at the request of the Orthodox parish of Sarajevo, with construc

candidates.name: Old Orthodox Church
candidates.alt: crkva sv. Arhanđela Mihaila i Gavrila
candidates.content: Also known as the Church of the Holy Archangels Michael and Gabriel (Cyrillic: црква св. Арханђела Михаила и Гаврила) is a Serbian Orthodox church. It was first mentioned in Ottoman sources dating to 1539. The church was built on

candidates.name: Church of St. Joseph
candidates.content: Roman Catholic church with 3 bells designed by Karel Pařík in a Romanesque Revival style, funded by Pope Pius XI. Construction began in 1936 and the building was consecrated in 1940, during the early months of the Second World War

candidates.name: Church of the Holy Transfiguration
candidates.content: Orthodox church designed by Alexander Deroko and built in 1940 in Byzantine Revival style. It was originally planned to be built in Split, owning its resemblance to similar buildings along the Adriatic coast, but eventually constr

candidates.name: Museum of Alija Izetbegović
candidates.content: Small museum within the Ploča and Širokac gates of Vratnik, dedicated to Alija Izetbegović, first president of the independent Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He served 1992-2000, much of that time only nominally as he was bes

candidates.name: Dariva Canyon
candidates.content: An 8 km long promenade from the historic centre of Sarajevo to the Goat's Bridge, following the canyon of the Miljacka. The promenade is very picturesque, and the pedestrian-only route offers magnificent natural views which have b

candidates.name: Spring of the Bosna River
candidates.price: 2 KM park admission, 2 KM/hour parking, 20 KM for a one way horse-and-carriage ride
candidates.content: The beginning of the river Bosna, where the pure and ice cold water surges out of the mountains. You can walk in the large, well-kept park, picnic and spend the whole day without getting bored. The 1st May festival, a public holid

candidates.name: Sunnyland
candidates.content: A newly constructed bobsleigh track on Mount Trebevic overlooking Sarajevo, and adjacent restaurants and bars selling food and drinks. Excellent entertainment for children, with indoor playgrounds and facilities.

candidates.name: National Theatre
candidates.content: The National Theatre has a regular programme of plays, concerts and opera. It was built in 1899 as a "Gentlemen's Club" by Czech architect Karel Pařík, who contributed to over 160 buildings in and around Sarajevo.

candidates.name: Olympic Stadium
candidates.alt: Koševo City or Asim Ferhatović - Hase Stadium
candidates.content: Multi-purpose arena built for the 1984 Winter Olympics, capacity 34,500, it's now the home ground of FK Sarajevo. They play in the top tier of national football, the Premier League of Bosnia and Herzegovina or "Liga 12". The natio

candidates.name: Sarajevo Zoo
candidates.price: 3 KM for adults, 2 KM for children
candidates.content: A small zoo and recreation park at the outskirts of Sarajevo, primarily aimed at children. It is the oldest zoo in Bosnia and Herzegovina. During the Austro-Hungarian period it was located in Ilidza. There are 57 species of animal

candidates.name: Stadium Grbavica
candidates.content: This is the home ground (capacity 16,000) of FK Željezničar Sarajevo, who likewise play in the top tier Liga 12.

candidates.name: Sarajevo Winter International Festival
candidates.content: Winter counterpart of the Film Festival, with music, visual arts, film and video, performing arts and literature, plus a program for children.

candidates.name: Sarajevo International Guitar Festival
candidates.content: Eminent guitar players lead concerts, workshops and competitions.

candidates.name: Sarajevo Film Festival
candidates.content: Large summer film festival, various venues including the outdoor "Summer Screen". The Culture Centre has a box office, but book online if you can.

candidates.name: MESS International Theatre Festival
candidates.content: Festival for expressive arts, with special attention to youth and alternative subjects.

candidates.name: Sarajevo Jazz Festival
candidates.content: Large eclectic jazz festival.

candidates.name: Cable car
candidates.price: 30 KM return, 20 KM one-way (locals pay less than a third)
candidates.content: Restored in 2018, this cable car runs up to the former . The area boasts views, hilltop strolls, and a decent cafè. However, the ride could be considered a bit overpriced. Forest paths lead to the Pino Hotel (accessible by road, e

candidates.name: Fox in a Box
candidates.content: Escape room games. In "Mr Fox's Secret Study", you try to escape from the office by solving riddles. In "The Bank Job", you try to steal diamonds from the bank safe, in the dark by torch. In "The Bunker", you try to avert an accid

candidates.name: Inside the Siege: Sarajevo's Story of Survival
candidates.content: Guided historical tour focused on the Siege of Sarajevo (1992–1996), the longest siege of a capital city in modern European history. The experience explores important wartime locations connected to daily life during the siege, inc

candidates.name: Skakavac Waterfall
candidates.content: Waterfall 12 km north of the city, above the Nahorevo Village. At 98 m in height, it is among the tallest waterfalls in Europe. Located in an area of exceptional natural beauty, surrounded by lush forests of spruce, beech and fir

candidates.name: Ilidza Thermal Riviera
candidates.price: Basic entry 9 KM, extra for wellness & fitness centres
candidates.content: Water park with several indoor and outdoor swimming pools, wave pool, massage amenities and water slides. Slightly outdated infrastructure, but the natural sulphur rich water makes up for it on hot summer days. Sauna and fitness c

candidates.name: Isa-begov Hamam
candidates.hours: Mon-Fri 10:00-13:30 for men, 14:00-18:00 for women, Sat 09:00-19:00 for women, Sun 09:00-19:00 for men
candidates.content: Renovated hamam in the Isa-begov Hotel with traditional Ottoman steam room, water pool and massage facilities.

candidates.name: Café de Paris
candidates.content: You might not have expected to find an IPA in the Balkans, but Café de Paris serves a selection of craft beers from Sarajevo microbreweries. They also have a range of very smooth local rakijas (try the quince). Riverside, outdoor

candidates.name: Opera Bar/Café
candidates.content: Fast WiFi connection, but the staff can be unfriendly and inattentive. Attracts a community of casual actors and musicians.

candidates.name: Ministry of Ćejf
candidates.content: Great espresso and well trained baristas. Also has karak and good cakes.

candidates.name: Tre Bicchieri Wine Store & Tasting Bar
candidates.content: Long list of Italian wines. Very cozy and comfortable place. Good music & relaxing atmosphere.

candidates.name: Miris Dunja
candidates.content: Coffee, including Bosnian coffee, and fruit juices. On a typical day the Bosnian coffee is very good, and on a good day it is extraordinary.

candidates.name: Cafe Slastičarna "Palma"
candidates.content: Coffee and pastry shop, located in the part of town called Hrasno, started in 1970. In 1985 "Palma" received the CD -Diplomatic Consular Code.

candidates.name: Mrvica
candidates.content: Coffee, brunch or even lunch

candidates.name: Mrvica Old Town
candidates.content: Coffee and different types of cakes and desserts. No Bosnian coffee served, only "modern" coffee styles.

candidates.name: House of Spite
candidates.content: The history of this restaurant dates back to the Austro-Hungarian occupation, when Sarajevo underwent large scale infrastructure projects which resulted in the post office, the National Museum, the Faculty of Law and many others.

candidates.sec: City centre around the Vječna vatra memorial
candidates.name: Srebrena školjka
candidates.content: Traditional Bosnian cuisine in a fabulous atmosphere, very very nice staff, almost like stepping back in time. If you're looking for a break from the hustle and bustle of the summer heat, this is it. The upstairs dining room has c

candidates.name: Petica Ferhatović
candidates.content: Popular but spacious serving fresh beef ćevapi. The waitresses wear traditional Bosnian dresses.

candidates.sec: City centre around the Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque
candidates.name: Fan Ferhatović
candidates.content: Pleasant ambience in the bazaar, good local food, friendly staff.

candidates.sec: City centre around the Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque
candidates.name: Ćevabdžinica Željo 3
candidates.content: Traditional Bosnian barbecue food. The atmosphere is great.

candidates.sec: City centre around the Vječna vatra memorial
candidates.name: Sedef
candidates.content: Traditional dishes, comfortable and quiet place in an alley. A very beautiful restaurant, the food is delicious and clean, and the service is amazing.

candidates.name: Pizzeria Maslina
candidates.content: Affordable with a diversity of cuisines, from Italian to Bosnian traditional food.

candidates.sec: City centre around the Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque
candidates.name: Teraza
candidates.content: Pizzas and Bosnian sandwiches. Excellent location just heart of the city center with unique retro design makes you feel calm and relax. The food and the service are good.

candidates.sec: City centre around the Vječna vatra memorial
candidates.name: Ćevabdžinica Nune
candidates.content: A little restaurant in the backyard of the main street Ferhadija. Super cute father and son shop with some of the best cevapci in town! Definitely a recommendation for a quick meal.

candidates.sec: City centre around the Vječna vatra memorial
candidates.name: Chipas
candidates.content: Excellent food, fast service, very cultured and friendly waiters, everything clean and tidy. A large selection of food and drinks at a very decent price.

candidates.name: Ascinica ASDž
candidates.content: When you get sick of greasy meats, ASDž serves Bosnian-home-cooking, vegetable-based dishes (but don't expect vegetarian, as many are still flavoured with little meat). Order cafeteria-style at the counter: you pay by the plate, a

candidates.name: A P Ǝ T I T
candidates.content: An "open kitchen" and a daily menu prepared from ingredients; meat dishes, fish dishes, risottos, pastas, imaginative salads, fragrant woks and delicious sweet pleasures. Also dishes for vegans, vegetarians and gluten-free offerin

candidates.name: Markale Market
candidates.content: Market hall opened in 1895 and home to local meat, cheese and vegetable merchants: walnuts are a speciality. The market was bombed with great loss of life in February 1994 and again in August 1995. The first attack was a single mo

candidates.name: Gazi-Husrev Beg's Bezistan
candidates.content: A covered market for haberdashery and craftsmanship, built during the Ottoman Empire period, with a design based on the design of the mosques. The bedesten serves as the central building in the historic commercial part of the city

candidates.name: Pijaca "Ciglane"
candidates.content: Interesting local market where you won't find any tourist.

december.text: Morića Inn: The only preserved Ottoman Inn (han literally means roadside inn) in Sarajevo, built in 1551, under the benevolence of Gazi Husrev-Beg's endowment (vakuf).
